summary: Phase J — Storefront Draft vs Live Visual Diff + Publishing workflow. Tested publish → list revisions → diff → revert → re-publish cycle (backend) and the PublishDiffDrawer (frontend). 8/9 backend tests pass; 1 reveals a real edge-case bug where snapshot freezes status='draft' before the publish updates the page to 'published', causing diff to report a phantom status change after a revert→publish sequence. Frontend drawer fully functional: tabs, view-mode toggle, empty-state, revisions list with Live chip + Revert buttons, label input, disabled Publish-now when no changes.

minor.issue: Snapshot is taken BEFORE the cms_pages.status is flipped to 'published'. If the page was in 'draft' (e.g. just after a revert), the frozen snapshot stores status='draft' while the live page becomes status='published'. Subsequent GET /diff?vs=published reports a phantom page.changed.status={from:'draft',to:'published'} and summary.has_changes=true, which will incorrectly light up the Studio dirty badge with 0 field changes. Repro: revert to any rev → publish → diff. Mitigation: either (a) move the snapshot AFTER the cms_pages.update in publish_page() in /app/backend/core/storefront_revisions.py, or (b) drop 'status' from PAGE_FIELDS_TO_FREEZE since it's a workflow field, not content, or (c) set snap['page']['status']='published' before insert.
Returns 400 instead of 404 for an unknown page_key (consistent with the validator but a 404 would be more REST-friendly).

action_items: Fix snapshot-status timing bug in /app/backend/core/storefront_revisions.py::publish_page so a fresh publish does not leave the page diff reporting a phantom status change.
Optional: return 404 instead of 400 for unknown page_key on the diff endpoint.
Cleanup: the demo tenant 'home' page now has ~9+ revisions including TEST_* labels from past iterations; consider periodic pruning.
critical_code_review_comments: core/storefront_revisions.py snapshot_page captures status which is a workflow flag — diffing it produces noise (see bug above).
publish_page's prev-snapshot diff for change_summary uses the LIVE page, not the new snapshot, which is fine but means change_summary may also include the same phantom status change.

revert_to_revision performs DELETE-then-INSERT of cms_sections without a transaction — a failure mid-flight would leave the page section-less. Consider wrapping in a Postgres function or supabase RPC for atomicity.
Public endpoint correctly serves from frozen snapshot (served_from='revision') and preview=1 returns served_from='draft' — verified.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Demo 'home' page left in CLEAN baseline state — final revision label 'clean-baseline-iter40' is the live revision and diff vs published shows has_changes=false.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_storefront_revisions.py covers publish/list/diff/modify-section/public-serve/revert/republish. Login response uses session.access_token (Supabase shape). The test_republish_cleanup test will fail until the snapshot-status timing bug is fixed (it asserts has_changes=false after a revert+publish sequence). Home page baseline is currently 'clean-baseline-iter40'.
rca of the issue: publish_page() in core/storefront_revisions.py runs snapshot_page BEFORE updating cms_pages.status to 'published'. The snapshot therefore freezes whatever status the page had at the moment of publish (e.g. 'draft' after a revert). Then publish bumps live page status to 'published'. Diff comparing live (published) to snapshot (draft) reports a status change that never reflects an actual content edit. Fix options: reorder (snapshot AFTER update), or remove 'status' from PAGE_FIELDS_TO_FREEZE, or patch snap['page']['status']='published' before persisting the revision.
